date_inferred_from: Dated by the Konin land court's decree of October 1777 (APP 53/6/0/-/46, document 2), which cites this transfer as acknowledged before the Pyzdry court on Wednesday, the eve of the Feast of the Nativity of the Virgin Mary, 1768: 7 September. The Pyzdry court's next sitting was on Friday 9 September 1768.
text:
No. 39: Excellens Joannes Traholtz Mercator et Incola Witkoviensi Sanus mente et Corpore existens Manifeste Recedendo &c[etera] Recognovit Quia Ipse Totus et integras summas suas proprias pecuniarias Unam quidem Mille Quinquaginta Trium Imperialium Grossorum Tredecim, Fenicorum[?] sex per olim Magnificum Paulum Prusimski pro arboribus per modernum Recognoscentem honoratum Traholtz in Borris et sylvis Trąpczynensi mediante Contractu in ordine emptionis earundem Arborum [ordine?] praefato olim Magnifico Prusimski conscripto proprio honorati Traholtz recognoscentis peculio curaque elaboratis (licet si olim idem Magnificus Prusimski ab eodem recognoscente plenariam ad sonantiam praemissi contractus satisfactionem perceperit) in dictis borris et sylvis Trąpczynensi per hancce olim Magnificum Prusimski eidem recognoscenti violento modo interceptis ac honorato Simonis Mercatori Stetinensi per eundem Magnificum Prusimski divenditis, in hocce quanto (Testante ejusdem honorati Simonis Mercatoris Stetinensis scripto reversali vulgo Auscuk[Auszug]) acceptam, Deinde alteram Mille Quingentorum Tredecim florenorum per eundem honoratum Traholtz recognoscentem modernum partim in confectionem secaminum id est Klapek novem Stru[i]um vulgo Rynek, itidem per olim Magnificum Antonium Prusimski ejusdem olim Magnifici Pauli Prusimski fratrem germanum ex ratione subsecuta Borrarum et sylvarum inter ipsos controversiae ac disquisitionis in haece borra interceptarum, per recognoscentem honoratum Traholtz erogatam partim pro commodo et interesse memorati olim Magnifici Pauli Prusimski expositam se[?]rsivo Regestro per huncce recognoscentem conscripto specificatam ac per huncce olim Magnificum Antonium Prusimski pro hisce secaminibus acceptam proque sisc[e?] ac commodo suo dispositam tum et alias summas scriptis et Documentis manualibus ac
Regestris tum variis connotationibus alisculi~ vocitatis explanatas recognoscentem jure legati respicientes nihil sibi et suis successoribus ex praedictis summis in post reservando et excipiendo in Personam Magnifici Stanislai Chełmski uti hisce summas iure[?] suo proprio sibi recognoscenti persolventis ac pro praemissis plenarie satisfacientis ejusque successorum pleno totali integroque jure suo Dominio proprietato et competentia una cum quibus quibusvis petendi ad hisce summas se referentibus et hasce summas enucleatibus un[s?][u?][o?]n provisionibus ab ejsdem summis capitalibus provenientibus ac[u?]um process[ae?] juris per Recognoscentem successoribus Prusimscianis instituto cessit contulit transposuit transtulit et transfudit prout cedit confert transponit transfert et transfundit Actaq[ue] praesenti Da[m/s?] et concedens [?] haec sua personali recog[ni]tioni ad praemissa libere accedente
Jan Traholtz ręką trzymaną
Sup[er] Transfusionem sui Juris in Per M. Chełmski

translation.en:
No. 39: The Excellent Jan Tracholz, merchant and inhabitant of Witkowo, sound in mind and body, openly, withdrawing, etc., acknowledged that he himself, wholly and entirely, his own monetary sums, one of them being 1,053 imperials, 13 groszy and 6 Pfennig[?], due from the late Right Honourable Paweł Prusimski, for trees bought by the present acknowledger, the honourable Tracholz, in the pine forests and woods of Trąbczyn by means of a contract written out for the said late Right Honourable Prusimski for the purchase of those same trees [...], worked out from the honourable acknowledger Tracholz's own funds and care (although the same late Right Honourable Prusimski had once received from the same acknowledger full satisfaction according to the tenor of the aforesaid contract), the trees having been seized from the same acknowledger by force in the said pine forests and woods of Trąbczyn by this late Right Honourable Prusimski and sold by the same Right Honourable Prusimski to the honourable Simon, merchant of Szczecin; received in this amount (as the written acknowledgement of the same honourable Simon, merchant of Szczecin, commonly called an *Auscuk* [the German Auszug, an extract of account], attests);

and then a second sum, of 1,513 złoty, spent by the same honourable Tracholz, the present acknowledger, partly on the making of sawn goods, that is, nine stacks of *Klapek* [a trade name of sawn timber], commonly called *Rynek*, likewise seized by the late Right Honourable Antoni Prusimski, full brother of the same late Right Honourable Paweł Prusimski, by reason of what followed upon the pine forests and woods in controversy and inquiry between them, seized in this pine forest; spent by the acknowledger, the honourable Tracholz, and partly laid out for the benefit and interest of the said late Right Honourable Paweł Prusimski, set out in a separate[?] register written by this acknowledger, and received for these sawn goods by this late Right Honourable Antoni Prusimski and disposed of for [...] and for his own benefit; and other sums, [shown] by writings and documents, handwritten ones and registers,

and also explained by various annotations, called [...]; these sums belonging to the acknowledger by right of legacy, reserving and excepting nothing from the aforesaid sums for himself and his successors thereafter, he has ceded, conferred, transposed, transferred and made over (as he cedes, confers, transposes, transfers and makes over) into the person of the Right Honourable Stanisław Chełmski, as one paying these sums to the acknowledger by his own right[?] and fully satisfying him for the foregoing, and to his successors, with full, total and entire right, dominion, ownership and competence, together with any and all rights of claiming that relate to these sums and set these sums out, together[?] with the interest arising from the same principal sums and with[?] the legal process instituted by the acknowledger against the successors of the Prusimskis; and by the present act [...] and conceding [...], this his personal acknowledgement freely assenting to the foregoing.

Jan Tracholz, by his held hand

On the transfer of his right in[?] the person of the Right Honourable Chełmski

summary_en: The merchant Jan Tracholz of Witkowo declares before the municipal court of Pyzdry that he makes over to Stanisław Chełmski, owner of Łukom beside Trąbczyn, who pays him for them, his own claims against the late Paweł Prusimski, heir of Trąbczyn. The first sum, 1,053 imperials, 13 groszy and (it seems) 6 Pfennig, concerns trees from the pine forests of Trąbczyn that Tracholz had bought under a written contract and which Paweł Prusimski seized from him by force and sold to a merchant Simon of Szczecin. The second, 1,513 złoty, Tracholz had spent partly on the making of sawn goods (nine stacks), which Paweł's late full brother, the elder Antoni Prusimski, likewise seized, and partly laid out for Paweł's benefit; other sums set out in his writings and registers go with them. With the claims Tracholz hands over the rights to them, the interest, and the proceedings he had begun against Paweł Prusimski's successors. Tracholz signs "by his held hand", another hand guiding his.
summary_de: Der Kaufmann Jan Tracholz aus Witkowo erklärt vor dem Burggericht in Pyzdry, dass er an Stanisław Chełmski, Besitzer von Łukom neben Trąbczyn, der ihn dafür bezahlt, seine eigenen Forderungen an den verstorbenen Paweł Prusimski, den Erben von Trąbczyn, abtritt. Die erste Summe, 1053 Imperialen, 13 Groschen und (wie es scheint) 6 Pfennig, betrifft Bäume aus den Kiefernwäldern von Trąbczyn, die Tracholz aufgrund eines schriftlichen Vertrags gekauft hatte und die Paweł Prusimski ihm gewaltsam wegnahm und an einen Kaufmann Simon aus Stettin verkaufte. Die zweite, 1513 Złoty, hatte Tracholz teils für die Herstellung von Schnittware (neun Stapel) aufgewendet, die Pawełs verstorbener leiblicher Bruder, der ältere Antoni Prusimski, ebenfalls wegnahm, teils zu Pawełs Nutzen ausgelegt; dazu kommen weitere Summen aus seinen Schriften und Registern. Mit den Forderungen übergibt Tracholz die Rechte daran, die Zinsen und das von ihm gegen Paweł Prusimskis Nachfolger eingeleitete Verfahren. Tracholz unterschreibt mit „gehaltener Hand“, von einer fremden Hand geführt.
